----------------------------------------------------------------------
This is the API documentation for the basemapper library.
----------------------------------------------------------------------


## Basemap views

Create a view (`basemap()`), change it (`set_view`, `set_bounds`), read it (`get_bounds`, `get_center`, `get_zoom`, `get_size`) and render it (`render_png`, `render_svg`, `render_array`). The same functions and arguments exist in R.



basemap(style: 'Union[StyleLike, Sequence[StyleLike]]', width: 'int' = 800, height: 'int' = 600, *, center: 'Optional[Tuple[float, float]]' = None, zoom: 'Optional[float]' = None, bounds: 'Optional[Any]' = None, crs: 'Optional[Any]' = None, pixel_ratio: 'float' = 1.0, layers: 'Optional[List[str]]' = None, labels: 'Union[bool, str]' = True, features: 'Optional[List[str]]' = None, auth_token: 'Optional[str]' = None, tile_timeout_ms: 'int' = 10000, max_tiles: 'int' = 256, tile_concurrency: 'int' = 16, fail_on_tile_error: 'bool' = False) -> 'Basemap'

Create a basemap view.

The view is a centre and MapLibre zoom (512 px tiles; fractional zooms are
rendered natively, not resampled), or bounds to fit. ``width`` and
``height`` are CSS pixels; images are ``pixel_ratio`` times larger with
the same view and label layout (MapLibre's ``devicePixelRatio``):
``pixel_ratio=2`` gives a sharp 2x image, ``pixel_ratio=dpi / 96`` matches
a print resolution. The same function exists in R (``basemap()``) and
Rust (``Basemap::new()``), with the same arguments.

Args:
    style: A MapLibre GL style URL or JSON string (e.g. from
        :func:`basemap_provider`), or a list of those stacked bottom to
        top (e.g. a basemap published as separate hillshade, base and
        label services).
    width: View width in CSS pixels.
    height: View height in CSS pixels.
    center: ``(longitude, latitude)`` of the view centre.
    zoom: MapLibre zoom (0-22, fractional allowed).
    bounds: Bounds to fit instead of ``center``/``zoom``: a
        ``[xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax]`` sequence (in ``crs``, default
        EPSG:4326), a dict, or a GeoDataFrame / GeoSeries.
    crs: CRS of ``bounds`` (anything ``pyproj.CRS`` accepts).
    pixel_ratio: Device pixels per CSS pixel.
    layers: Optional layer filter applied to every style: plain IDs keep
        only those layers, ``-`` prefixed IDs drop them; ``*`` and ``?``
        are wildcards (``"-label_*"``). See :func:`list_layers`.
    labels: ``True`` keeps every layer, ``False`` drops the labels (text
        and icons), ``"only"`` keeps only the labels on a transparent
        background, to stack over another map. Catalogue raster
        basemaps switch to their label-free or label-only tiles.
    features: Optional feature filter applied to every style: plain
        names keep those features, ``-`` prefixed names drop them, e.g.
        ``["water", "roads"]`` or ``["-buildings"]``. Features:
        background, water, landcover, parks, buildings, roads, rail,
        boundaries, places, poi, terrain, other (see the ``feature``
        of :func:`list_layers`).
    auth_token: Optional access token for the tile service.
    tile_timeout_ms: Per-tile HTTP timeout in milliseconds.
    max_tiles: Maximum tiles fetched per style.
    tile_concurrency: Parallel tile downloads.
    fail_on_tile_error: Abort on a failed tile instead of leaving it empty.

Returns:
    A :class:`Basemap`.

Example:
    >>> import basemapper
    >>> ugrc = "https://tiles.arcgis.com/tiles/99lidPhWCzftIe9K/arcgis/rest/services"
    >>> m = basemapper.basemap(
    ...     [f"{ugrc}/{s}/VectorTileServer/resources/styles/root.json"
    ...      for s in ("VectorHillshade", "LiteBase", "LiteLabels")],
    ...     800, 600, center=(-111.8887, 40.7556), zoom=12.4, pixel_ratio=2,
    ... )
    >>> m.render_png("slc.png")   # 1600 x 1200
    >>> m.render_svg("slc.svg")   # vector

Basemap(style: 'Union[StyleLike, Sequence[StyleLike]]', width: 'int' = 800, height: 'int' = 600, *, center: 'Optional[Tuple[float, float]]' = None, zoom: 'Optional[float]' = None, bounds: 'Optional[Any]' = None, crs: 'Optional[Any]' = None, pixel_ratio: 'float' = 1.0, layers: 'Optional[List[str]]' = None, labels: 'Union[bool, str]' = True, features: 'Optional[List[str]]' = None, auth_token: 'Optional[str]' = None, tile_timeout_ms: 'int' = 10000, max_tiles: 'int' = 256, tile_concurrency: 'int' = 16, fail_on_tile_error: 'bool' = False) -> 'None'

A map view rendered headlessly: one style, or several stacked.

Create one with :func:`basemap`; see there for the arguments. Change the
view with :meth:`set_view` / :meth:`set_bounds` (which return the view, so
calls chain), read it with the ``get_*`` methods, and render it with
:meth:`render_png`, :meth:`render_svg` or :meth:`render_array`.


## Basemap Methods

Methods for the Basemap class


set_view(self, center: 'Optional[Tuple[float, float]]' = None, zoom: 'Optional[float]' = None) -> "'Basemap'"

Set the centre ``(longitude, latitude)`` and/or the MapLibre zoom
(0-22, fractional allowed); ``None`` keeps the current value.

set_bounds(self, bounds: 'Any', crs: 'Optional[Any]' = None) -> "'Basemap'"

Fit the view to ``bounds`` (in ``crs``, default EPSG:4326), keeping
the view's size.

get_bounds(self, lonlat: 'bool' = False) -> 'Tuple[float, float, float, float]'

The view's ``(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)`` in EPSG:3857 metres, or in
degrees with ``lonlat=True``.

get_center(self) -> 'Tuple[float, float]'

``(longitude, latitude)`` of the view centre.

get_zoom(self) -> 'float'

The MapLibre zoom of the view.

get_size(self) -> 'Tuple[int, int]'

``(width, height)`` of rendered images in device pixels.

get_attribution(self) -> 'str'

The attribution text the view's styles ask maps to show (see
:func:`get_attribution`), e.g. for a caption.

__repr__(self) -> 'str'

render_array(self) -> 'np.ndarray'

Render to a ``(height, width, 4)`` uint8 RGBA array (device pixels).

render_png(self, path: 'Optional[str]' = None) -> 'bytes'

Render a PNG, written to ``path`` when given. Returns the PNG bytes.

render_svg(self, path: 'Optional[str]' = None, text: 'str' = 'editable', embed_fonts: 'str' = 'subset', font_dirs: 'Optional[List[str]]' = None) -> 'str'

Render a vector SVG (``width`` x ``height`` user units;
``pixel_ratio`` does not apply), written to ``path`` when given.
Returns the SVG text.

Args:
    path: Output file, or None.
    text: ``"editable"``: labels are ``<text>`` elements (editable,
        selectable) at MapLibre's glyph positions, halos as strokes,
        with the style's fonts embedded; labels whose font file is not
        available fall back to ``"bitmap"``. ``"bitmap"``: every label
        drawn from the style's own glyph bitmaps, thresholded by SVG
        filters as MapLibre's shader does (MapLibre's look at any
        zoom; not editable). ``"paths"``: glyph outlines traced from
        those bitmaps (plain paths, no filters).
    embed_fonts: ``"subset"`` (only the glyphs used), ``"full"``
        (whole fonts, for retyping labels) or ``"none"`` (fonts by
        name only). Fonts come from ``font_dirs``, the
        ``BASEMAPPER_FONT_DIRS`` folders, a local cache, then Google
        Fonts for open fonts; others are referenced by name.
    font_dirs: Folders of .ttf / .otf files to use first.


## One-shot rendering

Render bounds to an RGBA array in one call.


render_basemap_raw(bounds: 'Any', width: 'int', height: 'int', style: 'Any', crs: 'Optional[Any]' = None, pixel_ratio: 'float' = 1.0, tile_zoom: 'Optional[int]' = None, layers: 'Optional[List[str]]' = None, labels: 'Union[bool, str]' = True, features: 'Optional[List[str]]' = None, auth_token: 'Optional[str]' = None, tile_timeout_ms: 'int' = 10000, max_tiles: 'int' = 256, tile_concurrency: 'int' = 16, fail_on_tile_error: 'bool' = False) -> 'np.ndarray'

Render a basemap for bounds in one call.

A one-shot render: fit ``bounds`` into a ``width`` x ``height`` CSS-pixel
view and return the pixels. :func:`basemap` with
:meth:`Basemap.render_array` gives the same result with a reusable view.
The same function exists in R (``render_basemap_raw()``).

Args:
    bounds: Bounding box: a ``[xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax]`` sequence in
        ``crs`` (default EPSG:4326, with a warning when the values look
        projected), a dict with ``xmin``/``ymin``/``xmax``/``ymax`` (and
        optionally ``crs``) keys, or a GeoDataFrame / GeoSeries (CRS read
        from it).
    width: View width in CSS pixels.
    height: View height in CSS pixels.
    style: A MapLibre GL style URL or JSON string (e.g. from
        :func:`basemap_provider`), or a list of those stacked bottom to
        top.
    crs: CRS of ``bounds`` (anything ``pyproj.CRS`` accepts).
    pixel_ratio: Device pixels per CSS pixel; the image is
        ``width * pixel_ratio`` by ``height * pixel_ratio``.
    tile_zoom: Tile detail override: the tile zoom on the 256 px grid
        (vector sources use one less, their tiles being 512 px), or
        ``None`` to pick tiles as MapLibre does for the view.
    layers: Optional layer filter: plain IDs keep only those layers,
        ``-`` prefixed IDs drop them; ``*`` and ``?`` are wildcards
        (``"-label_*"``).
    labels: ``True`` keeps every layer, ``False`` drops the labels (text
        and icons), ``"only"`` keeps only the labels on a transparent
        background, to stack over another map. Catalogue raster
        basemaps switch to their label-free or label-only tiles.
    features: Optional feature filter applied to every style: plain
        names keep those features, ``-`` prefixed names drop them, e.g.
        ``["water", "roads"]`` or ``["-buildings"]``. Features:
        background, water, landcover, parks, buildings, roads, rail,
        boundaries, places, poi, terrain, other (see the ``feature``
        of :func:`list_layers`).
    auth_token: Optional access token for the tile service.
    tile_timeout_ms: Per-tile HTTP timeout in milliseconds.
    max_tiles: Maximum tiles fetched per style.
    tile_concurrency: Parallel tile downloads.
    fail_on_tile_error: Abort on a failed tile instead of leaving it empty.

Returns:
    numpy.ndarray: ``(height * pixel_ratio, width * pixel_ratio, 4)``
    uint8 RGBA pixels.

Raises:
    BasemapError: On any rendering or network failure.


## Plot integrations

Drop a basemap layer into an existing plot, rendered at the output resolution. `geom_basemap` takes the same arguments in plotnine and ggplot2 (R).



add_basemap(ax: "'matplotlib.axes.Axes'", style: 'Union[str, Any, Sequence[Any]]', tile_zoom: 'Optional[int]' = None, alpha: 'float' = 1.0, layers: 'Optional[List[str]]' = None, labels: 'Union[bool, str]' = True, features: 'Optional[List[str]]' = None, pixel_ratio: 'Optional[float]' = None, auth_token: 'Optional[str]' = None, tile_timeout_ms: 'int' = 10000, max_tiles: 'int' = 256, attribution: 'Union[bool, str]' = True, crs: 'Optional[object]' = None) -> "'xr.DataArray'"

Render a basemap beneath existing axes content.

The basemap is an artist that renders when the figure is drawn, at the
output resolution: on screen at the canvas dpi, and natively at the
requested resolution in ``savefig(dpi=...)`` or PDF / SVG output. Takes
the same arguments as :class:`geom_basemap` (and R's ``geom_basemap()``).

Args:
    ax: An existing matplotlib Axes.
    style: A MapLibre GL style URL or JSON string (e.g. from
        :func:`basemap_provider`), or a list of those stacked bottom to
        top.
    tile_zoom: Tile detail override: the tile zoom on the 256 px grid
        (vector sources use one less), or None to pick tiles as MapLibre
        does for the view.
    alpha: Opacity of the basemap layer (0.0–1.0).
    layers: Optional layer filter. Plain IDs keep only those layers;
        minus-prefixed IDs drop those layers; ``*`` and ``?`` are
        wildcards.
    labels: ``True`` keeps every layer, ``False`` drops the labels (text
        and icons), ``"only"`` keeps only the labels on a transparent
        background, to stack over another map. Catalogue raster
        basemaps switch to their label-free or label-only tiles.
    features: Optional feature filter applied to every style: plain
        names keep those features, ``-`` prefixed names drop them, e.g.
        ``["water", "roads"]`` or ``["-buildings"]``. Features:
        background, water, landcover, parks, buildings, roads, rail,
        boundaries, places, poi, terrain, other (see the ``feature``
        of :func:`list_layers`).
    pixel_ratio: Device pixels per CSS pixel (MapLibre's
        devicePixelRatio). Default: output dpi / 96, so lines and labels
        keep their physical size at any dpi. Larger values draw map
        symbols smaller.
    auth_token: Optional access token for the tile service.
    tile_timeout_ms: Per-tile HTTP timeout in milliseconds.
    max_tiles: Maximum tile downloads per style.
    attribution: The credit line the basemap's providers ask for, drawn
        small in the bottom-right corner over the plot: ``True`` (the
        default) for the styles' own (see :func:`get_attribution`),
        ``False`` for none, or your own text.
    crs: CRS of the axes data coordinates (anything ``pyproj.CRS``
        accepts, e.g. ``"EPSG:4326"``, ``gdf.crs``). Required for plain
        matplotlib axes and GeoDataFrame plots, whose axes carry no CRS;
        detected automatically for cartopy axes when omitted.

Returns:
    xarray.DataArray of shape (height, width, 4) holding the first render
    (at the figure's current dpi), with spatial bounds and CRS in
    ``.attrs``. The live artist is ``ax.images[-1]``.

Raises:
    BasemapError: If CRS detection fails, the render fails, or the network
        is unreachable.

geom_basemap(style: 'Any', tile_zoom: 'Optional[int]' = None, alpha: 'float' = 1.0, layers: 'Optional[List[str]]' = None, labels: 'Union[bool, str]' = True, features: 'Optional[List[str]]' = None, pixel_ratio: 'Optional[float]' = None, auth_token: 'Optional[str]' = None, tile_timeout_ms: 'int' = 10000, max_tiles: 'int' = 256, attribution: 'Union[bool, str]' = True, crs: 'object' = 'EPSG:4326', **kwargs: 'object') -> 'None'

Render a styled basemap beneath plotnine spatial layers.

Defers all tile fetching to draw time so that the plot's coordinate system
has been established. Uses the same injection logic as :func:`add_basemap`.

The basemap renders when the plot is drawn, at the output resolution
(natively at ``save(dpi=...)``), like :func:`add_basemap`. The same
layer exists in R (ggplot2 ``geom_basemap()``), with the same arguments.

Args:
    style: A MapLibre GL style URL or JSON string (e.g. from
        :func:`basemap_provider`), or a list of those stacked bottom to
        top.
    tile_zoom: Tile detail override: the tile zoom on the 256 px grid
        (vector sources use one less), or None to pick tiles as MapLibre
        does for the view.
    alpha: Opacity of the basemap layer (0.0–1.0).
    layers: Optional layer filter list — plain IDs keep only those layers;
        minus-prefixed IDs drop those layers; ``*`` and ``?`` are
        wildcards.
    labels: ``True`` keeps every layer, ``False`` drops the labels (text
        and icons), ``"only"`` keeps only the labels on a transparent
        background, to stack over another map. Catalogue raster
        basemaps switch to their label-free or label-only tiles.
    features: Optional feature filter applied to every style: plain
        names keep those features, ``-`` prefixed names drop them, e.g.
        ``["water", "roads"]`` or ``["-buildings"]``. Features:
        background, water, landcover, parks, buildings, roads, rail,
        boundaries, places, poi, terrain, other (see the ``feature``
        of :func:`list_layers`).
    pixel_ratio: Device pixels per CSS pixel; default output dpi / 96.
    auth_token: Optional access token for the tile service.
    tile_timeout_ms: Per-tile HTTP timeout in milliseconds.
    max_tiles: Maximum tile downloads per style.
    attribution: The credit line the basemap's providers ask for, drawn
        small in the bottom-right corner over the plot: ``True`` (the
        default) for the styles' own (see :func:`get_attribution`),
        ``False`` for none, or your own text.
    crs: CRS of the plot's x/y data (anything ``pyproj.CRS`` accepts).
        plotnine has no spatial coordinate system to read it from, so it
        defaults to ``"EPSG:4326"`` (longitude/latitude). Pass e.g.
        ``crs=gdf.crs`` or ``crs="EPSG:3857"`` for projected data.

Example:
    >>> import pandas as pd
    >>> from plotnine import ggplot, aes, geom_point
    >>> from basemapper import basemap_provider, geom_basemap
    >>> df = pd.DataFrame({"lon": [-111.95, -111.80], "lat": [40.68, 40.80]})
    >>> (ggplot(df, aes("lon", "lat"))
    ...  + geom_basemap("OpenFreeMap.Positron")
    ...  + geom_point())


## Styles

Named basemaps (leaflet-providers names, usable as `style`), styles for your own tile data, and OGC services. Tile data (tile URLs, TileJSON, PMTiles, ArcGIS services) also works as `style` directly.



basemap_provider(name: 'str', type: 'Optional[str]' = None, api_key: 'Optional[str]' = None, tiles: 'Optional[str]' = None, labels: 'Union[bool, str]' = True, features: 'Optional[List[str]]' = None) -> 'str'

A named basemap's style.

Names follow leaflet-providers (``"CartoDB.Positron"``,
``"Esri.WorldImagery"``, ``"OpenStreetMap.HOT"``); see
:func:`list_providers` or the :data:`providers` object. A name also works
as ``style`` directly; this function picks the form, passes a key, or
swaps in your own tiles.

Args:
    name: Basemap name (case-insensitive).
    type: ``"vector"`` (a MapLibre style) or ``"raster"`` (tiles). By
        default the vector form when there is one, else raster. Asking
        for a form a basemap lacks is an error, never a silent fallback.
    api_key: API key for CARTO, MapTiler and Stadia; by default read
        from ``CARTO_API_KEY``, ``MAPTILER_API_KEY`` or
        ``STADIA_API_KEY``. The keys are free for moderate use;
        :func:`list_providers` shows which basemaps need one.
    tiles: Your own tile data to draw with this basemap's style: a
        ``.pmtiles`` archive (URL or path), tile URL or TileJSON. It must
        use the same schema as the provider's tiles (OpenMapTiles for
        OpenFreeMap and Stadia).
    labels: ``True`` keeps every layer, ``False`` drops the labels,
        ``"only"`` keeps only the labels, to stack this basemap's labels
        over another map. Raster tiles switch to the provider's
        label-free or label-only tiles (an error when it has none).
    features: Vector form: features to keep (``["water", "roads"]``)
        or drop (``["-buildings"]``); see :func:`list_layers`.

Returns:
    A style URL, or inline style JSON (the raster form, or with
    ``tiles``, ``labels`` or ``features``).

Raises:
    ValidationError: For an unknown name (with suggestions), a form the
        basemap lacks, or a missing API key.

list_providers(type: 'Optional[str]' = None) -> 'List[Dict[str, object]]'

The basemaps :func:`basemap_provider` knows.

Args:
    type: ``"vector"`` or ``"raster"`` to list only basemaps with that
        form; None lists all.

Returns:
    One dict per basemap: ``name``, ``vector`` and ``raster`` (the forms
    it has), ``api_key_env`` (the environment variable its key is read
    from, or None when it needs none) and ``attribution``.

providers

Basemap names of one provider, as attributes.

tile_style(source: 'str', type: 'Optional[str]' = None, tile_size: 'Optional[int]' = None, scheme: 'Optional[str]' = None, minzoom: 'Optional[int]' = None, maxzoom: 'Optional[int]' = None, attribution: 'Optional[str]' = None, source_layers: 'Optional[List[str]]' = None, paint: 'Optional[Dict[str, object]]' = None, auth_token: 'Optional[str]' = None) -> 'str'

A style for tile data, with overrides.

``source`` is what you could pass as ``style`` directly; use this function
to override what is detected, or to get the style JSON to edit:

* a tile URL template (``{z}/{x}/{y}``, ``{quadkey}``,
  ``{bbox-epsg-3857}``, WMTS ``{TileMatrix}/{TileRow}/{TileCol}``);
* a TileJSON URL or file;
* a PMTiles archive: URL, local path or ``pmtiles://`` URL;
* an ArcGIS ``.../MapServer`` (raster tiles) or ``.../VectorTileServer``
  (its published style);
* a style URL or file (returned with relative URLs made absolute).

Raster tiles get one raster layer. Vector tiles get a default style
drawing every source layer (polygons as translucent fills, lines and
outlines, points as circles, a colour per source layer) over a
transparent background.

Args:
    source: The tile data, as above.
    type: ``"raster"`` or ``"vector"``; detected when None (from the
        archive header, the TileJSON, the URL's extension, or one fetched
        tile).
    tile_size: Raster tile size in px (default 256 for tile URLs and
        archives).
    scheme: ``"xyz"`` or ``"tms"`` (rows counted from the south).
    minzoom: Minimum zoom of the tiles.
    maxzoom: Maximum zoom of the tiles (overzoomed beyond).
    attribution: Attribution text for the source.
    source_layers: Vector tiles: the source layers to draw (default all).
    paint: Vector tiles: paint properties for the generated ``fill-*``,
        ``line-*`` and ``circle-*`` layers, e.g. ``{"fill-color": "#ccc"}``.
        Others are dropped with a warning.
    auth_token: Optional access token for the tile service.

Returns:
    The style JSON.

Raises:
    ValidationError: If the type cannot be detected or does not match the
        data, or ``source`` is not found.

wms_style(url: 'str', layers: 'str', styles: 'str' = '', version: 'str' = '1.3.0', format: 'str' = 'image/png', transparent: 'bool' = False, extra_params: 'Optional[str]' = None) -> 'str'

Style for an OGC WMS GetMap endpoint, as 256 px tiles in EPSG:3857.

Args:
    url: Base service URL without query parameters.
    layers: ``LAYERS`` parameter.
    styles: ``STYLES`` parameter.
    version: Service version (1.1.x sends ``SRS``, 1.3.0 ``CRS``).
    format: Image MIME type.
    transparent: Request transparent images.
    extra_params: Additional query parameters appended verbatim.

wmts_style(url: 'str', layer: 'str', tilematrixset: 'str' = 'GoogleMapsCompatible', format: 'str' = 'image/png', style: 'str' = 'default', version: 'str' = '1.0.0', extra_params: 'Optional[str]' = None) -> 'str'

Style for an OGC WMTS GetTile (KVP) endpoint. A RESTful WMTS
template (``{TileMatrix}/{TileRow}/{TileCol}``) needs no builder: pass it
as ``style``.

Args:
    url: Base service URL without query parameters.
    layer: ``LAYER`` parameter.
    tilematrixset: Tile matrix set (a Web Mercator one).
    format: Image MIME type.
    style: ``STYLE`` parameter.
    version: Service version.
    extra_params: Additional query parameters appended verbatim.


## Style layers and attribution

A style's layers with their features, for the `layers` and `features` filters, and the attribution text it asks maps to show.



list_layers(style: 'Any', auth_token: 'Optional[str]' = None, layers: 'Optional[List[str]]' = None, labels: 'Union[bool, str]' = True, features: 'Optional[List[str]]' = None) -> 'List[Dict[str, Optional[str]]]'

List a style's layers, or preview a filter.

The layers of a style in drawing order: their ``id`` (what ``layers``
matches), ``type`` (``symbol`` layers are the labels ``labels`` keeps or
drops), ``source_layer`` (the vector tile layer drawn, None for
background and raster layers) and ``feature`` (what ``features``
matches). With ``layers``, ``labels`` or ``features``, the layers a
render with those filters draws; an empty list when they leave nothing.
The same function exists in R (``list_layers()``, returning a data
frame).

A layer's feature comes from its source layer, with tables for the
OpenMapTiles (OpenFreeMap, Stadia, MapTiler), Protomaps (CARTO) and
Shortbread (VersaTiles) schemas, and keywords for others (Esri's
descriptive names, layer ids). It is a convenience: check it here, and
use ``layers`` for exact control.

Args:
    style: A style (anything :func:`basemap` takes).
    auth_token: Optional access token for the style URL.
    layers: Layer filter to preview: plain IDs keep, ``-`` prefixed IDs
        drop; ``*`` and ``?`` are wildcards.
    labels: ``True``, ``False`` or ``"only"``, as the renderers take it.
    features: Feature filter to preview, as the renderers take it.

Returns:
    A list of ``{"id", "type", "source_layer", "feature"}`` dicts
    (``pandas.DataFrame(...)`` turns it into a table).

Raises:
    BasemapError: If the style cannot be fetched or parsed, or a filter
        is invalid.

get_attribution(style: 'Any', auth_token: 'Optional[str]' = None) -> 'str'

The attribution text a style asks maps to show.

Every source the style's layers draw from contributes its attribution
(from the style, the source's TileJSON or PMTiles metadata), as MapLibre's
attribution control collects it, as plain text without duplicates, joined
with ``" | "``. Use it for a caption or a credit line, e.g.
``ax.annotate(get_attribution(style), ...)``. :meth:`Basemap.get_attribution`
gives a view's. The same function exists in R (``get_attribution()``).

Args:
    style: A style (anything :func:`basemap` takes), or a list of
        styles stacked bottom to top.
    auth_token: Optional access token for the tile service.

Returns:
    The attribution; an empty string when the styles give none.


## Tile cache


tile_cache(dir: 'Optional[str]' = None, clear: 'bool' = False) -> 'Optional[str]'

The disk cache for map tiles.

Tiles are kept as long as the server's caching headers allow (a day when
they say nothing), so repeated renders of an area do not download them
again. The cache starts in ``BASEMAPPER_CACHE_DIR`` when set (``off``
disables it), else in the platform cache directory.

Args:
    dir: Move the cache to this directory; ``False`` or ``""`` turns it
        off. None leaves it as it is.
    clear: Delete every cached tile.

Returns:
    The cache directory, or None when the cache is off.


## Exceptions


BasemapError(message: str) -> None

Base exception for all basemapper errors.

ValidationError(message: str) -> None

Raised for invalid bbox, dimensions, zoom, or layer filter.

Subclasses both :class:`BasemapError` and :class:`ValueError` so that
callers that catch the built-in ``ValueError`` continue to work unchanged.

StyleError(message: str) -> None

Raised when a style cannot be fetched or parsed.

NetworkError(message: str) -> None

Raised when tile or style network requests fail.
